title: ALMA 2D super-resolution imaging survey of Ophiuchus Class I/flat spectrum/II disks. I. Discovery of new disk substructures
question: Do Class I, Flat Spectrum and Class II disks in Ophiuchus show substructures, and when do they appear, as revealed by SpM super-resolution imaging of archival ALMA Band 6 data?

data.sensitivity: sigma = 0.16 mJy/beam in initial CLEAN images

what.value: L_bol, T_bol and alpha_IR for all systems

evidence.quote: We referred to (cite: Dunham_2015) for $L_{\rm bol}$ and $T_{\rm bol}$ of all the systems.

what.value: eDisk T_bol and dust disk radii

evidence.loc: 5.1 Comparison with Targets in eDisk Project
evidence.quote: The bolometric temperatures $T_{\rm bol}$ and dust disk radii $R_{\rm disk}$ for the eDisk samples are taken from (cite: Yen_2024_edisk).

recipe.method: tclean with Briggs robust 0.5, MFS nterm=2; SNR-dependent self-calibration
key_parameters: 5 sigma detection, sigma=0.16 mJy/beam; SNR>20 selection

recipe.method: l1+TSV regularized imaging with 10-fold cross validation; Lambda_tsv increased by 10x for 11 sources with patchy structure
2D Gaussian fit to SpM images with MCMC; ellipse fit for 13 ring disks

recipe.goal: Disk radii by curve of growth
recipe.method: Deproject, azimuthally average, integrate to get R68% and R95%; uncertainty = geometric mean theta_eff/(2 sqrt(2 ln2))
Radial and major-axis intensity profiles classified as Smooth, Ring, Inflection, Spiral

recipe.goal: Statistics vs T_bol, R_dust and inclination
recipe.method: KS tests; Monte Carlo (10000 iterations) KS tests of cos i vs uniform
assumptions: cos i uniform in 0-1 for random orientation

answer_key.quantity: Median resolution improvement of SpM vs CLEAN

evidence.quote: The SpM images achieve an effective spatial resolution that is a median of 3.8 times higher than that of the CLEAN images.

evidence.loc: 4.1 Measurements and Statistical Analysis of Disk Sizes
evidence.quote: with medians of 18 and 27 au, respectively
We classify the disks as follows: 43 ‘Smooth’, 26 ‘Ring’, one ‘Spiral’, and 5 ‘Inflection’.
we detected 32 disks with distinct substructures (‘Ring’, ‘Spiral’, and ‘Inflection’), accounting for 41% of all detected disks

answer_key.quantity: KS p-value Class I/FS vs Class II inclination

evidence.loc: 5.2 Selection Bias of Disk Evolutionary Stages

answer_key.quantity: Ring probability Class I, FS, II

evidence.quote: The probabilities of Class I, Class FS, and Class II disks having ring structures are 40%, 33%, and 38%, respectively
